item.title: Ask HN: Can we do a karma reset? (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: The high karma accounts are not always smart people, usually they're incredibly immature and clearly lacking in experience. Often, an account like this will post a comment demonstrating they have no clue what they're talking about, and when someone even lightly corrects them what happens? They immediately abuse their power with heavy downvotes and sock puppets they can easily promote with their heavily weighted votes. This is a shit-for-brains cliquey strategy that makes the site worse than it could otherwise be. What would it take to do a 1-time karma reset (or has it already happened)? It could be a way to save the site, otherwise I fear people will eventually jump ship. The site format is fine, UI/UX, etc. but a few bad apples here spoil the whole bunch and they are multiboxing accounts like crazy to shape the narrative in highly personal, egoic, selfish ways that hurt the site and content just to comfort their ego by giving them undeserved authority. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49673488 Points: 5 # Comments: 1

item.title: Show HN: Bodily Oddities (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: When I was about 11 years old, my best friend and I were playing during recess at school, and I was carrying him around on my back, presumably pretending to be a multipart attack robot. All of a sudden, my heart started hurting, and I collapsed to my knees, and the robot was no more. Every time I inhaled, it would feel like a spike was being driven into my heart, and my breathing got completely shallow. I was sure I was done for, when all of a sudden, after an exhale, it disappeared. It wasn't until I was in my twenties that I learned this was called Precordial catch syndrome and it happens to most everyone. Every friend I've told about it was surprised, and also most knew the feeling. I collected a growing list of strange things bodies do ever since. And now finally I made it into a little page for others to see: https://vester.si/bodily-oddities/ It includes a form to tell me about new things, if you think they belong on the page. Feedback welcome! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49649789 Points: 305 # Comments: 189
